group.passage: Humpback whales are famous for jumping high above the waves and hitting the water with their long fins. Some swim about 5,000 miles each year between warm waters, where they give birth, and cold waters, where they feed on krill and small fish. Each whale can even be recognized by the black-and-white pattern under its tail, which scientists use to tell one animal from another. For much of the 20th century, however, these giants were hunted on an industrial scale. The chart shows how many whales of all kinds were killed around the world in each decade. Humpbacks were only one of many targets, but they suffered badly: before the hunting stopped, most of their populations had shrunk by more than 95 percent. Off the coast of Brazil, the story was especially dramatic. About 25,000 humpbacks were caught there in roughly 12 years in the early 1900s, and by the 1950s only about 450 remained. As scientists noticed numbers falling worldwide, humpbacks were given protection in the 1960s. Then, during the mid-1980s, the International Whaling Commission declared a pause on all commercial whaling, which offered the struggling whales further safety. It worked better than many experts expected. An earlier assessment had suggested that the Brazilian population had recovered to only about 30 percent of its original size. But a 2019 study, using more complete records of past catches, estimated that it had grown back to some 25,000 whales, or about 93 percent of its numbers before hunting began. Under United States law, nine of the world's 14 humpback populations are no longer listed as endangered or threatened. The comeback is not complete. Humpbacks still get caught in fishing gear, struck by ships, and disturbed by underwater noise. Their return may also raise new questions, since whales compete with penguins and seals for the same krill. Even so, the humpback has become proof that a species pushed to the edge can recover when people stop killing it.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about humpback whales, according to the passage?

options.B: They give birth in the same cold waters where they feed.
options.C: They were the only whales hunted on an industrial scale.
options.D: They feed mainly on penguins and seals in cold waters.

options.B: Fewer whales were killed in the 2000s than in the 1990s.

3.strategy_zh: 指涉題可以從後文驗證：It worked better than expected 之後舉的是族群回升的證據，所以 It 一定是「能產生效果的措施」，再回到前兩句找出那一整件事。

translation_zh.text:
座頭鯨以躍出水面、用長長的鰭拍打水面而聞名。有些座頭鯨每年在溫暖和寒冷的海域之間游大約 5,000 英里；牠們在溫暖的海域生產，在寒冷的海域以磷蝦和小魚為食。每一頭鯨甚至可以從尾巴下方的黑白花紋認出來，科學家就靠這些花紋分辨不同的個體。

然而，在 20 世紀的大部分時間裡，這些巨獸遭到工業規模的獵捕。圖表顯示每個十年全世界被捕殺的各種鯨魚數量。座頭鯨只是眾多獵捕目標之一，卻受害慘重：在獵捕停止之前，大多數座頭鯨族群都減少了 95% 以上。

在巴西外海，情況特別驚人。1900 年代初期，那裡在大約 12 年間捕獲了約 25,000 頭座頭鯨，到了 1950 年代只剩下大約 450 頭。由於科學家注意到全世界的數量都在下降，座頭鯨在 1960 年代受到保護。接著在 1980 年代中期，國際捕鯨委員會宣布暫停所有商業捕鯨，讓這些苦苦掙扎的鯨魚得到更多保障。

這些措施的效果比許多專家預期的還要好。先前的一項評估認為，巴西的族群只恢復到原本規模的大約 30%。但 2019 年的一項研究使用更完整的過去捕獲紀錄，估計這個族群已經回升到大約 25,000 頭，約為獵捕開始前數量的 93%。依美國法律，全世界 14 個座頭鯨族群中，已有 9 個不再被列為瀕危或受威脅。

這場復甦還沒有完成。座頭鯨仍會被漁具纏住、被船隻撞擊，並受到水下噪音的干擾。牠們的回歸也可能帶來新的問題，因為鯨魚會和企鵝、海豹爭奪同樣的磷蝦。即便如此，座頭鯨已經證明：一個被逼到絕境邊緣的物種，只要人類停止捕殺，就能夠恢復。

【圖 1】全世界每十年被捕殺的鯨魚數量（各物種合計）：1900 年代 52,110 頭、1910 年代 177,557、1920 年代 229,100、1930 年代 403,287、1940 年代 256,989、1950 年代 613,862、1960 年代 703,235（最高）、1970 年代 363,661、1980 年代 77,074、1990 年代 10,300、2000 年代 18,141、2010 年代 14,957。1990 年以前只計工業化的商業捕鯨；1990 年起的數字也包含原住民為了食物而進行的捕鯨。
